message.content:
Sure! You can ask the API to return **only** the `id` and `context` fields for the CAA records of `sample2.com`.  
Just use the *List* endpoint (`GET /v1/records/caa`) and supply the `fields` query‑parameter (or the equivalent header).  

Below are two quick ways to do it – one with `curl`, the other with plain Python `requests`.

---

## 1️⃣ Using `curl`

```bash
curl \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer secret567" \          # <-- your API key
  "https://api.example.com/v1/records/caa?domain=sample2.com&fields=id,context"
```

> **What this does**  
> * `domain=sample2.com` tells the API which zone to look at.  
> * `fields=id,context` limits the response to just those two properties.  
> * The `Authorization` header passes your API key securely.

If you prefer passing the key as a query parameter instead of a header, you can drop the `Authorization` header and append `&api_key=secret567` to the URL:

```bash
curl "https://api.example.com/v1/records/caa?domain=sample2.com&fields=id,context&api_key=secret567"
```

---

## 2️⃣ Using Python `requests`

```python
import requests

api_key = "secret567"
base_url = "https://api.example.com/v1/records/caa"

headers = {
    "Accept": "application/json",
    "Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}",   # <-- your API key
}

params = {
    "domain": "sample2.com",
    "fields": "id,context",                # <-- only these fields
}

resp = requests.get(base_url, headers=headers, params=params)
resp.raise_for_status()                    # raise an error if the call failed

data = resp.json()
print(data)                                 # prints a list of dicts with only id & context
```

> **Result**  
> The JSON returned will look something like this:

```json
[
  {
    "id": "caasample2com-12345",
    "context": {
      "name": "sample2.com",
      "created_at": "2024-01-15T12:34:56Z",
      "updated_at": "2024-02-20T09:10:11Z"
    }
  },
  ...
]
```

Only the `id` and `context` keys appear; everything else is omitted.

---

### Quick Recap

| What you need | How to do it |
|---------------|--------------|
| **Endpoint** | `GET https://api.example.com/v1/records/caa` |
| **Domain filter** | `?domain=sample2.com` |
| **Field selection** | `&fields=id,context` |
| **Auth** | Header `Authorization: Bearer secret567` (recommended) or query `&api_key=secret567` |

That’s all you have to do to pull back just the IDs and context attributes for the CAA records of `sample2.com`. Happy querying!
